note: Hand-authored. Not an authority over gameplay semantics, and no longer a
home for the interaction contract: Slice 1 moved that into
OperationDefinition, where it has exactly one owner. This file now records
only how well each operation's declared contract is actually evidenced.
proof_status meanings: source_proven = follows from readable source;
unit_proven = a deterministic test pins it; live_proven = a named run
bundle shows it; unproven = declared, no proof yet; withheld = should not
No group-scope behaviour is live_proven anywhere in this repository. Every
was captured with exactly one character selected, so multi-recipient
semantics remain declared rather than demonstrated.

evidence: docs/generated/OPERATION_DEFINITIONS.md visible_controls boundary: activation proves delivery and a later observation, not the gameplay meaning of the result
entries.note: Section 10.4 forbids this remaining a universal gameplay escape hatch. It has no semantic contract because its effect boundary is deliberately generic; Slice 7 either narrows it to bounded UI delivery or removes the offer. Prospect is the concrete case that must not be activated through it.

The inventory window belongs to one character. Whether that character is Kenshi's primary or the first selected roster member is the section 13.7 proof; today affordances.py resolves it by roster iteration, which is the defect.
Mixed-building group behavior is unknown: recipients inside different buildings, or some already outside, have never been observed.

One planner-visible intent whose phases have different scopes. Its contract declares current_selection, but harvest_resource_is_currently_authorable still hard-requires a singleton selection - a gate that belongs to the late inventory-transfer phase, not to travelling or mining. Slice 1 stopped the menu offering it to a group it would refuse; it did not make a group able to harvest. Section 10.5 and Slice 6 own phase-scoped descriptors and the actual capability.

A directional walk plausibly broadcasts to the whole selection in Kenshi, but that has not been proven here. Before Slice 1 its cardinality gate made it unauthorable whenever a pair was selected, while still appearing on the planner's menu.
Group arrival semantics and per-recipient aggregation are unproven. Section 13.1 is its proof.

evidence: KenshiAgentTelemetry.cpp shift_into_body: PlayerInterface::recruit for a cross-faction body, createSquad + setFaction so the body is its own unit, updatePlayerSelection across the container move, then _selectPlayerCharacter(modifier=false, track=true) for exclusive primary selection

evidence: KenshiLib ZoneManager::getResource/getResourceBase is the resource field the Prospecting window reads
native survey completes on publication and issues no order, so it commands no recipient
entries.note: Reads Kenshi's resource field around the primary character and returns a grid rather than the window's area-averaged scalar, which reports 0 for a discrete deposit. Gated on an action deliberately: the agent learns what it surveyed, not what exists everywhere. Two things are unproven and are live-proof items - whether the null biome argument is accepted at runtime, and what the returned value scale means.

Issues a delayed interior-leg continuation through newPlayerTaskSelectedCharacters, so it is the clearest case for the captured dispatch basis and the ScopedOrderDispatcher. Section 13.3 is its proof.

evidence: docs/generated/GAME_BINDING_PARITY.md distinguishes witnessed from unwitnessed bindings
entries.note: Cannot have one universal contract merely because every case shares an input mechanism. Select All is the concrete case: it is currently offered by collecting the whole roster, and section 10.3 requires withholding it until live proof establishes whether the binding is active-platoon scoped.

evidence: operation_definitions.py WAIT_DEFINITION is internal-only run control
entries.note: Waiting is only meaningful while the world runs; the playback requirement is the honest declaration of that, not a licence to toggle pause.
